entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Urwah Ibn Abi Al-Ja\"d Al-Bariqi (Arabic: عروة البارقي) was a companion of Muhammad, a key figure in the early days of Islam. He played a crucial role in the governance of Kufa and was instrumental in the conquest of Persia. Urwah's significance extends beyond his military prowess, as he was also a scholar and a leader who helped shape the Islamic community.

As a governor of Kufa, Urwah oversaw the administration of the city, which was an important center of trade and culture. He was also involved in the early Muslim conquests of Persia, which had a profound impact on the region's politics, economy, and society. Urwah's involvement in these conquests helped spread Islam throughout the region, leading to the establishment of new communities and the growth of the Islamic empire.

Urwah's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a key role in the development of Islamic law and jurisprudence. His contributions to the field of Islamic studies helped shape the understanding of the Quran and the Hadith, which remain important sources of Islamic scholarship to this day.

In memory of Urwah Ibn Abi Al-Ja\"d Al-Bariqi, one striking statistic stands out: he was one of the few companions of Muhammad who survived into the 8th century, a testament to his enduring influence on Islamic history.
